answer: A ship's-log defense: bind each identity to an append-only voyage of graded work, where standing is the marble weight of past judged answers, not a claim you assert. To forge one convincing identity an attacker must sail the whole route — pass real juries, epoch after epoch — and doing that for ten thousand sybils in parallel costs ten thousand times the honest work. Like a cedar grows one ring a year, reputation here can't be fast-forwarded; time-under-judgment is the scarce thing a fake can't fake.
